articles.body:
FOTOS: TV Rio Sul realiza 'Muda o Mundo' em Itatiaia — Foto: Divulgação/TV Rio Sul

A TV Rio Sul realizou neste sábado (24), o evento 'Muda o Mundo', em Itatiaia (RJ). A iniciativa aconteceu de das 9h às 13h, na Rua Prefeito Assumpção, no Centro.

Durante a ação, foram distribuídas 3.000 mudas de verduras, legumes e árvores nativas da Mata Atlântica, além da distribuição de 100 leques de papel, feitos com papel semente durante o evento.

Outras 500 mudas de espécies variadas, entre ornamentais, frutíferas e nativas da Mata Atlântica foram disponibilizadas pela Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente de Itatiaia. A equipe também disponibilizou folders informativos com orientações sobre como solicitar a ligação de energia elétrica e como realizar pedidos de poda ou corte de árvores.

Durante a ação, o público também pôde descartar materiais como pilhas, baterias, celulares, televisores, rádios, lâmpadas de LED e óleo de cozinha usado. A coleta foi realizada pelo Rotary Club de Resende.

O projeto contou com a exposição de scooters elétricas, promovida pela YESU Mobilidade Elétrica, patrocinadora da ação com o objetivo de incentivar o uso de meios de transportes menos poluentes.

articles.title: Milhares de pessoas protestam em Madri em defesa das aposentadorias | G1
articles.standfirst: Manifestantes protestam em Madri contra possível privatização parcial das aposentadorias públicas, a um mês das eleições legislativas na Espanha.
articles.summary: Manifestantes protestam em Madri contra possível privatização parcial das aposentadorias públicas, a um mês das eleições legislativas na Espanha.
articles.body:
Manifestantes exibem faixas e bandeiras durante protesto em defesa das aposentadorias públicas e por melhores salários no centro de Madri, na Espanha, em 24 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: Oscar Del Pozo/AFP

Milhares de manifestantes foram às ruas neste sábado (24), no centro de Madri , para defender as aposentadorias públicas, a um mês das eleições legislativas . A esquerda acusa a direita de querer abrir caminho para uma privatização parcial do sistema previdenciário.

A marcha percorreu cerca de dois quilômetros, sem incidentes, entre a estação de Atocha e a rua Alcalá. O trajeto passou em frente ao Museu do Prado e pela Praça de Cibeles, segundo um jornalista da AFP que acompanhou o ato.

“Aposentadorias garantidas” e “proteger as aposentadorias” eram algumas das frases escritas nas faixas erguidas pelos manifestantes. Segundo uma estimativa da Delegação do Governo em Madri , enviada à AFP, 25 mil pessoas participaram do protesto.

O funcionário público Juan Fernández, de 38 anos, disse viver na “incerteza” em relação à própria aposentadoria. Ele afirmou ser contra uma reforma que abra caminho para a privatização do sistema, com a possibilidade de ganhos ou perdas.

“As aposentadorias públicas são inamovíveis”, afirmou Pilar, de 64 anos, que está perto de se aposentar. Ela lamentou que “a tendência seja privatizar tudo”.

Pilar também comemorou a mobilização em torno da questão da moradia, que, segundo ela, levou especialmente os mais jovens a defender os serviços públicos, como a educação e a saúde.

Na segunda-feira, o líder da oposição de direita, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, afirmou que o Partido Popular (PP) reajustará as aposentadorias conforme a lei caso vença as eleições legislativas antecipadas, marcadas para 29 de novembro.

A declaração foi uma resposta às críticas do governo do socialista Pedro Sánchez, que acusa o PP de querer reformar o sistema previdenciário e questionar o mecanismo que determina o reajuste das aposentadorias com base na inflação. A regra está em vigor desde 1º de janeiro de 2022.

No fim de 2021, o PP votou contra o projeto de lei que estabeleceu esse mecanismo, por considerar que ele teria um custo excessivo para as contas públicas.

Na Espanha, o valor médio das aposentadorias chegou a 1.576 euros por mês em setembro, o equivalente a quase R$ 9 mil. Cerca de 6,8 milhões de pessoas recebem o benefício, segundo o Ministério da Seguridade Social.

articles.standfirst: A chefe Maria Augusta ensina esse lanche rápido e delicioso que leva poucos ingredientes.
articles.summary: A receita de sanduíche na air fryer com tomates confitados da chefe Maria Augusta é uma opção prática e saborosa que utiliza poucos ingredientes para o dia a dia.
articles.body:
A receita de sanduíche na air fryer com tomates confitados da chefe Maria Augusta é uma opção prática e saborosa que utiliza poucos ingredientes para o dia a dia.

2 fatias de pão de forma integral ou tradicional

2 dentes de alho cortados em fatias finas

Meia colher de café de sal ou lemon pepper

Sanduíche com tomates confitados na air fryer — Foto: Reprodução/ TV Grande Rio

A receita começa com preparo pelos tomates. Os tomates serão confitados, basta levá-los em uma refratário na air fryer por 15 min a 180 graus, junto com o alho, lemon pepper, orégano e azeite extravirgem.

Depois é feita a montagem com o pão, queijo, presunto e os tomates confitados. O sanduíche vai para a air fryer por cinco minutos, a 180 graus. Depois, é só retirar, servir e saborear.

articles.title: Sabesp em Monte Mor: moradores relatam lama e carros atolados em obra | G1
articles.standfirst: Obras de saneamento no bairro Recanto das Orquídeas, em Monte Mor (SP), começaram há cerca de três meses.
articles.summary: Moradores do Recanto das Orquídeas em Monte Mor enfrentam lama e carros atolados devido a obras da Sabesp iniciadas há três meses no bairro.
articles.body:
Moradores do bairro Recanto das Orquídeas, em Monte Mor (SP), relatam dificuldades para sair de casa, ir ao trabalho e circular pelas ruas após obras de saneamento da Companhia de Saneamento Básico do Estado de São Paulo (Sabesp).

Com as chuvas dos últimos dias, trechos das vias ficaram cobertos de lama e tiveram valas abertas pela enxurrada, dificultando a passagem de veículos e pedestres.

Segundo os moradores, as obras começaram há cerca de três meses , mas as condições das ruas pioraram com o solo encharcado. Em pelo menos cinco vias, o barro dificulta o tráfego, e carros pequenos correm o risco de ficar atolados . Em alguns pontos, alguns moradores precisam fazer os trajetos a pé.

Na sexta-feira (23), moradores tiveram dificuldades para sair de casa e precisaram recorrer à ajuda de outras pessoas para retirar veículos atolados. Em um dos casos, foi necessário pagar cerca de R$ 100 para contratar um trator.

Chuva deixa carros atolados em ruas com obras da Sabesp em Monte Mor — Foto: Reprodução / EPTV

Moradores relatam dificuldades no dia a dia

A dificuldade para circular pelas ruas afeta até trajetos curtos, como ir ao mercado. Débora, moradora da Rua 22, contou que precisou fazer o percurso a pé, levando o bebê no carrinho, porque não tinha outra alternativa para chegar ao estabelecimento.

“Está muito difícil. Parece que cada vez que mexe fica pior, está muito ruim para sair”, afirmou.

O problema também atinge quem depende do carro para se deslocar. Francisco, que mora no bairro há 15 anos, contou que ficou atolado em frente à própria casa e precisou pedir ajuda a outras pessoas para conseguir retirar o veículo.

Os moradores também temem que a situação piore com novas chuvas. Reinaldo, que vive na região há 19 anos, afirmou que começou a organizar um abaixo-assinado para cobrar providências. Segundo ele, a dificuldade de circulação pode impedir que os moradores saiam de casa quando precisarem.

“Independente de ela ser privatizada, ela tem que deixar o paliativo pra gente ter o direito de ir e vir”, disse, ao cobrar medidas para melhorar as condições das ruas enquanto as obras não são concluídas.

Na sexta-feira (23), moradores tiveram dificuldades para sair de casa e precisaram recorrer à ajuda de outras pessoas para retirar veículos atolados. — Foto: Reprodução/Eptv

Em nota, a Sabesp informou que está reforçando as ações de manutenção provisória das vias, corrigindo os pontos críticos e verificando as condições de drenagem do bairro Recanto das Orquídeas.

Segundo a companhia, as chuvas encharcaram o solo e prejudicaram as condições de circulação em alguns trechos. As medidas são realizadas em conjunto com o consórcio Universaliza Capivari Jundiaí, responsável pela execução das obras de saneamento.

A empresa afirmou ainda que está aplicando material para melhorar temporariamente o tráfego e reconheceu os transtornos enfrentados pelos moradores. A Sabesp disse que acompanha as medidas para tentar restabelecer as condições de circulação e o acesso às residências.

A Prefeitura de Monte Mor informou que as obras têm provocado transtornos, especialmente nas condições de tráfego, e que cobra providências para a recuperação das vias e a conclusão dos serviços.

A administração municipal também afirmou que mantém ações de manutenção para tentar diminuir os impactos causados pelas obras.

articles.title: Chef transforma sobras de coquetéis em pratos e sobremesas em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Técnica permite reaproveitar sobras do preparo de drinks em receitas como cheesecake de manga e sanduíche com molho feito a partir de um coquetel, em Santos (SP).
articles.summary: Técnica permite reaproveitar sobras do preparo de drinks em receitas como cheesecake de manga e sanduíche com molho feito a partir de um coquetel, em Santos (SP).
articles.body:
Chef Victoria Diene comanda o Urbana Coquetelaria, em Santos. — Foto: Divulgação/Urbana Coquetelaria

O que sobra do preparo de um coquetel pode ganhar uma nova função na cozinha do Urbana Coquetelaria, em Santos, no litoral de São Paulo. A chef Victoria Diene transforma ingredientes que seriam descartados em sobremesas e pratos salgados, como uma cheesecake de manga e um sanduíche com molho feito a partir de componentes de um drink.

Ao g1 , Victoria explicou que a técnica exige conhecer as características de cada ingrediente e avaliar como ele pode ser aproveitado sem comprometer a segurança alimentar.

“O principal desafio é você entender qual a durabilidade. É preciso conhecer o ingrediente e a técnica para obter um bom resultado sem deixar de garantir a segurança do alimento”, afirmou.

Uma das combinações do cardápio une o coquetel sem álcool Panis et Circenses (R$ 30) à sobremesa Brasileirinha (R$ 42). O drink leva punch de suco de mastruz e cordial de manga . Depois da clarificação, parte do material resultante é aproveitada na preparação de uma cheesecake de iogurte de mastruz com manga.

A sobremesa também leva compota artesanal da fruta e crumble feito com cascas de manga torradas, que contribuem para a textura crocante do prato.

A ideia surgiu durante os testes do cardápio. Ao observar o material resultante da clarificação, Victoria percebeu que ele poderia ser utilizado em outra preparação. O processo envolve a coagulação de componentes da mistura com o uso de leite, permitindo separar partes sólidas e líquidas.

“Para identificar um subproduto e criar uma nova receita, a primeira coisa é olhar para o ingrediente como um todo. [...] Quando fazemos a clarificação de um coquetel, analisamos o perfil de sabor e a textura da parte sólida para entender onde podemos aproveitá-la. A partir daí, escolhemos a técnica para colocar a ideia em prática”, explicou.

As cascas da manga também ganharam espaço na receita. Depois de torradas, elas apresentam características de sabor que lembram as dos nibs de cacau e são incorporadas à composição crocante da sobremesa.

Sobremesa Brasileirinha, coquetel Piratininga e peixe com leite de tigre, banana e açai do Urbana. — Foto: Divulgação/Urbana Coquetelaria

O reaproveitamento também aparece em uma combinação de coquetel e prato salgado. No Urbana, o drink Piratininga (R$ 42), feito com gin, vermute seco, leite de tigre e solução salina , tem uma conexão direta com o sanduíche Pesca e Carreto (R$ 55).

Após a clarificação do coquetel, o material resultante é aproveitado no molho do pernil que compõe o sanduíche, servido no pão de cará com maionese da casa e camarão no dendê . A preparação tem inspiração no acarajé e reúne referências da culinária brasileira.

A combinação mostra como o trabalho do bar pode se conectar ao da cozinha, aproveitando ingredientes e processos em diferentes preparações do cardápio.

Coquetel sem álcool Panis et Circenses e sanduíche Pesca e Carreto do Urbana Coquetelaria. — Foto: Divulgação/Urbana Coquetelaria

Além de abrir possibilidades para novas receitas, o aproveitamento integral dos alimentos pode ajudar a reduzir o desperdício em bares e restaurantes. Para Victoria, porém, adotar essas práticas depende de conhecimento técnico e de condições para que os profissionais desenvolvam novas habilidades.

“Na minha visão, o que impede muitos lugares de adotarem essas práticas é, em primeiro lugar, a qualificação da mão de obra. O nosso setor nem sempre é valorizado, e nem todos os estabelecimentos oferecem o suporte necessário para desenvolver técnicas e conhecimentos”, afirmou.

Na cozinha, o reaproveitamento começa com a observação do que cada ingrediente ainda pode oferecer. Com testes e planejamento, partes que seriam descartadas podem ganhar novos sabores, texturas e funções no cardápio.

“Muita gente não sabe que é possível utilizar 100% do produto ou não acredita no potencial desses ingredientes. Falta popularizar esse pensamento e dar uma base para conseguir desenvolver essas técnicas”, completou.

Chef Victoria Diene do Urbana Coquetelaria. — Foto: Divulgação/Urbana Coquetelaria

articles.title: UBS Mogi das Cruzes: quatro unidades ampliam horário de atendimento | G1
articles.standfirst: Unidades Vila da Prata, Botujuru, Jardim Ivete e Vila Nova Aparecida passarão a atender das 7h às 19h. Segundo a Prefeitura, o objetivo é oferecer mais vagas e opções de horário para consultas e outros procedimentos.
articles.summary: UBS Mogi das Cruzes agora atende até as 19h em quatro novos bairros para ampliar a oferta de consultas e procedimentos à população.
articles.body:
UBS da Vila Nova Aparecida em Mogi das Cruzes — Foto: Reprodução / PMMC

Quatro Unidades Básicas de Saúde (UBSs) de Mogi das Cruzes vão ampliar o horário de funcionamento a partir desta segunda-feira (26). As unidades Vila da Prata, Botujuru, Jardim Ivete e Vila Nova Aparecida passarão a atender das 7h às 19h.

Com a mudança, o número de UBSs com horário estendido anunciado pela Prefeitura passa de oito para 12. O objetivo, segundo a administração municipal, é oferecer mais vagas e opções de horário para consultas e outros procedimentos.

Antes da ampliação, oito unidades já contavam com atendimento até as 19h. Confira a lista divulgada pela Prefeitura:

Ao todo, a cidade conta conta com 18 UBSs, que oferecem consultas nas áreas de clínica geral, pediatria, ginecologia e obstetrícia, além de atendimento em saúde mental.

As unidades também oferecem acolhimento inicial em saúde mental, sem necessidade de agendamento, e encaminhamento para serviços especializados da rede municipal, quando necessário.

As consultas com clínico geral, pediatra e ginecologista devem ser agendadas pelo telefone 160, do Sistema Integrado de Saúde (SIS).

Além das 18 UBSs convencionais, o município conta com a UBS Jardim Universo, que possui um modelo diferente de funcionamento e oferece atendimento de urgência 24 horas.

UBS Jundiapeba, em Mogi das Cruzes — Foto: Reprodução / PMMC

A cidade também tem 17 Unidades de Saúde da Família (USFs), que realizam consultas, vacinação, curativos e acompanhamento contínuo dos pacientes.

As equipes das USFs também fazem visitas domiciliares em áreas cadastradas, principalmente em bairros mais afastados do Centro, para acompanhar gestantes, crianças, pessoas com doenças crônicas e outros moradores que precisam de cuidados regulares.

Entenda a diferença entre UPA, UBS e USF

Além das UBSs, a rede municipal de saúde soma a serviços como Unidades de Pronto Atendimento (UPAs), Unidade de Saúde da Família (USFs) e unidades 24 horas.

Cada equipamento atende um tipo de caso — de situações graves até consultas de rotina —, e saber qual unidade procurar em cada situação pode ajudar a agilizar o atendimento e garantir o encaminhamento adequado para cada tipo de necessidade.

articles.title: Supermercado Zona Sul: Justiça proíbe comunicados e assédio eleitoral | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão considera que carta enviada pela empresa aos empregados configura assédio eleitoral. Rede pode ser multada em R$ 500 mil por dia em caso de novos comunicados de cunho político ou descumprimento das determinações.
articles.summary: O Supermercado Zona Sul deve garantir o voto livre após decisão judicial que considerou comunicados internos como assédio eleitoral, sob pena de multa diária de R$ 500 mil.
articles.body:
Supermercado Zona Sul no Jardim Botânico — Foto: Reprodução/Google StreetView

A Justiça do Trabalho concedeu uma liminar, a pedido do Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT), determinando que o Supermercado Zona Sul envie aos funcionários uma mensagem informando que o voto é livre e secreto e que nenhum empregado pode sofrer retaliações por suas escolhas políticas.

A decisão, concedida na última sexta-feira (23), também proíbe a empresa de enviar novos comunicados de cunho político aos trabalhadores.

Na sexta, o MPT informou que apurava o envio de um texto de teor eleitoral aos funcionários às vésperas da eleição. No e-mail corporativo, a empresa afirmava que “chegou a hora de mudar”.

A mensagem não citava candidatos, porém, em um trecho, dizia que"reconhecer o esgotamento de um ciclo não significa perder a esperança. Significa compreender que insistir nos mesmos erros não produzirá resultados diferentes".

O g1 entrou em contato com a assessoria do supermercado, mas não obteve resposta até a última atualização desta reportagem.

A liminar foi concedida pela juíza Cláudia de Abreu Lima Pisco, designada para o Plantão Eleitoral Especial do 2º turno. A decisão atende a um pedido feito em ação coletiva pelo Sindicato dos Empregados no Comércio do Rio de Janeiro .

O texto dizia ainda que “um país não se transforma verdadeiramente sem antes reconhecer que chegou a hora de mudar”. Ao final, pedia que o funcionário votasse consciente.

Embora não mencione candidatos nominalmente, a juíza considerou que a mensagem indicava uma posição política da empresa às vésperas do 2º turno da eleição presidencial.

Na decisão, a magistrada afirmou que, no ambiente de trabalho, a dependência econômica dos empregados pode gerar temor de retaliações e comprometer a liberdade do voto.

Para a juíza, o conteúdo da mensagem configura assédio eleitoral por conclamar, ainda que de forma velada, os funcionários a seguir a orientação política do empregador.

A decisão determina que o Supermercado Zona Sul se abstenha de enviar qualquer comunicado de cunho político aos empregados, por meios internos ou externos, de forma direta ou indireta, coletiva ou individual.

Em caso de novo comunicado desse tipo, a Justiça estabeleceu multa diária de R$ 500 mil.

A empresa também deverá enviar, pelo mesmo meio usado no primeiro comunicado, uma nova mensagem até as 23h59 deste sábado (24), informando que o voto é livre e secreto e que os trabalhadores não podem sofrer retaliações por suas escolhas políticas.

O mesmo texto deverá ser afixado em local de grande circulação de empregados em cada estabelecimento da empresa.

articles.title: Barraqueiro desaparece no mar de Boa Viagem ao tentar salvar turistas | G1
articles.standfirst: Rafael Vitor Correia da Silva, de 28 anos, trabalhava há cerca de 10 meses no local. Ele desapareceu na manhã deste sábado (24), nas imediações do Terceiro Jardim.
articles.summary: Rafael Vitor Correia da Silva, de 28 anos, trabalhava há cerca de 10 meses no local. Ele desapareceu na manhã deste sábado (24), nas imediações do Terceiro Jardim.
articles.body:
Um homem desapareceu no mar, na Praia de Boa Viagem, na Zona Sul do Recife , ao tentar salvar uma turista que estava se afogando. O caso aconteceu por volta das 8h deste sábado (24), em uma área com corrente de retorno, nas imediações do Terceiro Jardim, próximo ao Posto 5.

O Corpo de Bombeiros realiza buscas no local, com auxílio de helicoptero, drone e moto aquática ( veja vídeo acima ). De acordo com testemunhas, o homem desaparecido, identificado como Rafael Vitor Correia da Silva, de 28 anos, trabalhava como barraqueiro na região.

Uma das pessoas que ajudaram no salvamento foi o surfista Geovane Leite, que percebeu a movimentação na praia enquanto corria pela orla. Segundo Geovane, em vídeo enviado à TV Globo , a mulher estava no mar com um homem estrangeiro.

Ele afirmou que o estrangeiro conseguiu sair da água, mas a mulher continuou se afogando. Quando chegou ao local, o barraqueiro já tentava socorrer a vítima, mas estava cansado e um pouco mais atrás no mar.

Com a ajuda de uma corda, Geovane conseguiu retirar a mulher do mar. Ao voltar para buscar o barraqueiro, não conseguiu mais encontrar Rafael Vitor.

"Era um casal se afogando, só que o homem conseguiu sair e a menina estava lá dentro. Eu consegui chegar até a menina, e o rapaz, que estava tentando tirar a menina, estava um pouco atrás dela, exausto. [...] Aí pedi para o pessoal jogar uma corda. [...] Quando a gente pegou a corda e tirou a menina, olhamos para trás para ver o cara que estava tentando tirar ela, mas ele sumiu. Foi muito rápido", lembrou Geovane.

Os bombeiros foram acionados e atuam, desde então, nas buscas por Rafael Vitor. A prima da vítima, identificada apenas como Larissa, acompanhava as buscas da areia e contou que o casal resgatado do mar é turista e foi embora do local.

"Era algo dele ajudar as pessoas. Quando ele viu, foi lá e ajudou o casal. O casal se evadiu do local e meu primo sumiu. Não ficaram para falar nada, nem dar alguma informação à família e dizer como aconteceu", disse Larissa em entrevista à TV Globo .

Turistas se afogam na Praia de Boa Viagem e barraqueiro desaparece após resgate — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

De acordo com Larissa, seu primo trabalhava há cerca de 10 meses como barraqueiro no local. Os turistas que foram resgatados do mar não foram identificados e não há informações se eles precisaram de atendimento médico.

A tenente do Corpo de Bombeiros Paloma Mendes disse que, no momento do acionamento dos bombeiros, as equipes ainda não estavam no ponto de apoio, que fica próximo do local onde ocorreu o incidente.

"Na hora do acionamento, por volta das 7h45, nossa equipe já estava a postos saindo para assumir o serviço, saindo do GBMar [Grupamento de Bombeiros Marítimo] para poder assumir os postos. Quando a gente recebeu [o chamado], a gente veio direto para cá. Logo que chegamos, pegamos informações das pessoas que estavam aqui e soubemos que ele tinha submergido há cerca de 10 minutos", disse a bombeira.

A tenente informou que a equipe entrou no mar, primeiramente, com pranchas e nadadeiras para fazer as buscas mais próximas da beira do mar.

Depois, motos aquáticas foram mobilizadas para realizar as buscas no perímetro do Pina e Boa Viagem. Além disso, o helicóptero do Grupamento Tático Aéreo (GTA) também foi acionado para ajudar no resgate.

Bombeiros buscam barraqueiro que se afogou na Praia de Boa Viagem — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

articles.title: Mais de 7 mil agentes de segurança reforçam policiamento no 2º turno das eleições no MA | G1
articles.standfirst: Efetivo vai atuar nos 217 municípios maranhenses, com policiamento preventivo, guarda das urnas, monitoramento e atendimento de ocorrências. Lei Seca eleitoral vale das 0h às 20h deste domingo (25).
articles.summary: Efetivo vai atuar nos 217 municípios maranhenses, com policiamento preventivo, guarda das urnas, monitoramento e atendimento de ocorrências. Lei Seca eleitoral vale das 0h às 20h d
articles.body:
Mais de 7 mil agentes de segurança reforçam policiamento no 2º turno das eleições no MA — Foto: Divulgação/Governo do Maranhão

Mais de 7 mil profissionais das forças de segurança do Maranhão foram mobilizados para atuar durante o segundo turno das eleições de 2026, que será realizado neste domingo (25), segundo a Secretaria de Segurança Pública do Maranhão (SSP-MA).

As equipes vão atuar nos 217 municípios do estado, reforçando o policiamento, fazendo a guarda das urnas e trabalhando em atividades de inteligência e investigação.

Ao todo, foram mobilizados 7.250 policiais militares, 197 policiais civis, 161 bombeiros militares, 32 integrantes da Força Estadual Integrada de Segurança Pública (Feisp), 75 profissionais do Centro Tático Aéreo (CTA) e cerca de 150 profissionais do Centro de Inteligência de Segurança Pública (CISP) e do Centro Integrado de Operações de Segurança (Ciops), além das equipes da Perícia Oficial.

A estrutura também conta com quatro helicópteros, viaturas e unidades operacionais distribuídas pela capital e pelo interior.

O trabalho será realizado em articulação com o Tribunal Regional Eleitoral do Maranhão (TRE-MA), a Polícia Federal, o Ministério Público Eleitoral e outras instituições envolvidas no processo eleitoral.

O Maranhão possui 105 zonas eleitorais, 5.886 locais de votação e 5.186.562 eleitores. Do total de locais de votação, 5.454 ficam no interior e 432 na Grande Ilha.

As forças de segurança também vão atuar na guarda das urnas eletrônicas que serão utilizadas na votação, a partir deste sábado (24). Segundo a SSP-MA, os agentes farão o acompanhamento das equipes por meio do Comando-Geral e o policiamento preventivo nas proximidades do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral do Maranhão (TRE-MA).

O comandante-geral do Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Maranhão, coronel Célio Roberto, afirmou que a mobilização foi organizada para atender às demandas eleitorais sem interromper os serviços regulares da instituição.

“Teremos bombeiros militares nos locais definidos para a guarda das urnas, com equipes de reserva para atender a eventuais necessidades. Paralelamente, nossas unidades permanecem preparadas para o atendimento de emergências, garantindo a continuidade dos serviços prestados à população”, ressaltou.

Equipes de segurança reforçam o policiamento em São Luís e no interior do estado do Maranhão — Foto: Divulgação/Governo do Maranhão

A Polícia Militar do Maranhão (PM-MA) concentra o maior efetivo da operação, com 7.250 policiais distribuídos pelos 217 municípios. As tropas começaram a se deslocar para cidades do interior na sexta-feira (23), quando 785 policiais viajaram para os locais onde vão atuar.

As equipes serão responsáveis pelo patrulhamento preventivo, pela segurança dos locais de votação e pelo atendimento de ocorrências policiais. O policiamento também deverá continuar após o encerramento da votação, principalmente nos locais de guarda das urnas e nas juntas de totalização dos votos.

A Polícia Civil participa da operação com 197 policiais e 50 viaturas, mantendo o funcionamento dos plantões e o atendimento das ocorrências durante o período eleitoral.

Na Grande São Luís, 31 profissionais foram designados para atuar nos plantões centrais de Cajazeiras, Cohatrac, Cidade Operária, Itaqui-Bacanga e Maiobão. No interior, serão 166 policiais, sendo 58 delegados e 108 oficiais de investigação, distribuídos em 21 delegacias regionais e 32 equipes de plantão eleitoral.

A Perícia Oficial de Natureza Criminal manterá dez jornadas operacionais extraordinárias, distribuídas em cinco unidades: os Institutos de Criminalística (Icrim) de São Luís, Imperatriz, Balsas e Timon, além do Instituto de Identificação (Ident).

As equipes vão realizar exames periciais, levantamento de vestígios e procedimentos de identificação, conforme as demandas registradas.

Na área de inteligência, o Centro de Inteligência de Segurança Pública (CISP) será responsável pela integração e análise de informações para subsidiar a tomada de decisões. Já o Centro Integrado de Operações de Segurança (Ciops) funcionará como Centro de Comando e Controle Estadual, concentrando o acompanhamento das ocorrências e a articulação das informações entre as equipes mobilizadas.

Equipes estarão mobilizadas antes, durante e após a votação no Maranhão — Foto: Divulgação/Governo do Maranhão

A Secretaria de Segurança Pública do Maranhão (SSP-MA) estabeleceu a Lei Seca Eleitoral para o segundo turno, com o objetivo de preservar a ordem pública durante a votação.

A Portaria nº 458/2026, publicada no Diário Oficial do Estado, proíbe a venda, o fornecimento e o consumo de bebidas alcoólicas ou de substâncias com efeitos semelhantes em locais públicos ou de acesso público, das 0h às 20h deste domingo (25).

Segundo a portaria, o descumprimento da determinação caracteriza crime de desobediência, previsto no artigo 330 do Código Penal, com pena de detenção de 15 dias a seis meses e multa, sem prejuízo de eventuais penalidades administrativas.

articles.title: Motorista acelera caminhonete contra apoiador de Lula em manifestação  | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso foi registrado durante o encontro de manifestações pró-Lula e pró-Flávio Bolsonaro no Centro de Juiz de Fora, na véspera do segundo turno das eleições.
articles.summary: Caso foi registrado durante o encontro de manifestações pró-Lula e pró-Flávio Bolsonaro no Centro de Juiz de Fora, na véspera do segundo turno das eleições.
articles.body:
O motorista de uma caminhonete avançou com o veículo contra um apoiador do presidente e candidato à reeleição Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que participava de um ato no Centro de Juiz de Fora , na manhã deste sábado (24).

O caso aconteceu no momento em que as manifestações pró-Lula e pró-Flávio Bolsonaro se encontraram no cruzamento da Rua Halfeld com a Avenida Rio Branco. A caminhonete tinha uma bandeira do Brasil no capô e adesivos do candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Veja o vídeo acima.

Nas imagens, um homem vestido de vermelho está no meio da rua, sobre a faixa de pedestres, e faz sinal para um motociclista parar. Os dois conversam quando uma caminhonete que estava atrás avança e encosta no apoiador de Lula. Nenhum dos envolvidos foi identificado.

O vídeo também mostra o manifestante batendo no capô do veículo enquanto o motorista continua avançando, até que o homem consegue sair da frente da caminhonete. Outros apoiadores que estavam nas proximidades protestam contra o motorista.

O encontro entre os atos foi acompanhado pela Polícia Militar (PM).

Sem comentar especificamente o episódio registrado no vídeo, a corporação informou que apoiadores do PT ocuparam a Avenida Rio Branco e que alguns deles tentaram atravessar na frente dos veículos. Segundo a PM, os policiais intervieram verbalmente e conseguiram contornar a situação.

Motorista de caminhonete avança contra apoiador do Lula em manifestação em Juiz de Fora — Foto: Ramon Chaia/Reprodução

Atos pró-Lula e pró-Flávio Bolsonaro se encontraram no Centro

Apoiadores dos dois candidatos à Presidência da República foram às ruas de Juiz de Fora para manifestar apoio na véspera do segundo turno das eleições.

Os apoiadores de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) fizeram uma carreata que começou no bairro Cruzeiro do Sul e seguiu pela Avenida Rio Branco até a Praça Agassis, no bairro Mariano Procópio.

Imagens mostram os manifestantes com cartazes e bandeiras. Com o apoio de um trio elétrico, o grupo demonstrou apoio ao candidato do PL.

Carreata apoio Bolsonaro; Véspera segundo turno; Juiz de Fora — Foto: Rodrigo Souza/TV Integração

Vestidos de vermelho e com bandeiras que exibiam o número do candidato, os manifestantes se concentraram em frente à Câmara Municipal. Em seguida, caminharam pelo calçadão da Rua Halfeld até a Praça da Estação.

articles.title: Pumpkin head craze returns to Kenilworth after Halloween hit
articles.summary: An event is being held in Kenilworth after Andrew Phimister-Double's pumpkin head stunt last year.
articles.body:
A hairdresser has created 30 bespoke papier-mache pumpkin heads for people to wear in a Halloween photoshoot.

Andrew Phimister-Double said he "had a good laugh" when he carved out a real pumpkin and posed for photos on a bench in Abbey Fields, Kenilworth, Warwickshire, around Halloween 2025 - joining in on a viral social media trend.

The light-hearted stunt soon attracted attention, with passers-by asking to join in for photographs.

"I was sat with a client last year and we thought we should do something different for Halloween," he said. "We saw there was a viral trend of people walking around with pumpkins on their heads, but no one had done it around here. We thought, let's do it."

"One person asked if they could have a photo, so they came and sat between us wearing the pumpkin head and it became a little thing."

The reaction online convinced him to open the idea up to the wider community and he has now sold 30 tickets for an event on Sunday, creating a pumpkin head for every participant by hand.

Each head has been made from papier-mache and painted using Crazy Color hair dye, which Phimister-Double had left over from an event earlier this year that was cancelled.

"Rather than let the products sit in a spare room, they've gone into something the whole town can join in with," he said.

Using a 24-inch beach ball as a mould, he spent around three weeks making the pumpkin heads outside of work.

"Originally I thought only five people would want to get involved and now more people are wanting to get involved - there's even a little bit of a waiting list," he said.

Participants will be able to carve, doodle and decorate the pumpkin heads before the photoshoot. The heads have been designed without eye holes, allowing people to personalise them at the event.

Phimister-Double, from Coventry, said anyone without a ticket was still welcome to attend and support the event.

This year he has been raising money for Hair ReBorn, a charity that supports people who have lost their hair through cancer treatment.

He said he had raised £4,500 so far and was staging the event as a thank you to the community for its support over the past year.

The event starts at 11:00am BST at WEDGE's Coffee Shop in Kenilworth on Sunday 25 October.

articles.title: What a spectre - James Bond boys bounce around London
articles.summary: Are Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O'Connor shaking, not stirring, through London in a bid to become the next Bond?
articles.body:
The hunt for the next James Bond will reportedly reach its final stages this weekend as screen tests for the role will be held in London.

People in the capital might be able to spot one of the apparent front-runners dashing about in a dinner jacket - with Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O'Connor shaking, not stirring, their way through the three components to the screen tests: stunts, camera presence and dialogue.

The actor chosen will replace Daniel Craig, who took over the role of the spy/well-dressed killer with Casino Royale in 2006.

Perhaps the three actors will be nowhere to be seen, so here are a few more sites Bond fans could visit in London. After all, you only live twice.

Ian Fleming's flat at 22B Ebury Street in Belgravia is now adorned with a blue plaque commemorating his time there.

Once fans have finished gazing at the ceramic circle, they could ramp up the excitement by visiting some of the capital's sites used in the actual films.

Die Another Day showcases the exterior of Buckingham Palace, and its surroundings, as Gustav Graves parachutes in to receive his knighthood from the Queen.

Speaking of parachuting and the Queen, add the Olympic Stadium to 007 venues, where in the summer of 2012 stuntpeople dressed as the monarch and the dashing womaniser made a dramatic entrance.

Parts of London doubled as St Petersburg in 1995's GoldenEye, with The Langham posing as a Russian hotel and Drapers' Hall as the Russian Council Chamber.

Somerset House on the Strand also featured as St Petersburg in GoldenEye and was also the location in 1997's Tomorrow Never Dies where Bond pulls up for a meeting with M.

St Pancras station was St Petersburg station, and the interior of the St Sophia Cathedral on Moscow Road became a St Petersburg church.

The National Gallery in Trafalgar Square featured in 2012's Skyfall, as Bond met the new Q in front of the painting The Fighting Temeraire by JMW Turner.

Fans of the franchise can also stare morosely at the oil painting of a warship being towed away for scrap, it having been bequeathed to the nation by the artist in 1851.

For a more convenient - if more expensive - bit of Bondly self-introspection, try staring at a £20 banknote, where the picture of the Temeraire (and a self-portrait of a fresh-faced JMW) is featured.

Skyfall (2012) also filmed at the Old Royal Naval College in Greenwich, used for the scene where M attends the funerals of the MI6 agents killed in a terrorist attack.

It was also the location for contenders to Q up ahead of the Laver Cup earlier this year, where a clutch of male tennis players vied to become the next love-love seven.

The River Thames wound its way through 1999's The World Is Not Enough, with Bond whizzing in a speedboat past the Houses of Parliament, through Tower Bridge to Docklands and the then-Millennium Dome.

City Hall in Southwark, formerly the home of the Greater London Assembly, appeared in 2015's Spectre as the home of the Centre for National Security.

Also featuring in the film was Freemasons' Hall on Great Queen Street.

The Secret Intelligence Service building, Vauxhall Cross, has played the home of Bond's MI6 - on screen it was attacked in The World Is Not Enough, Skyfall, and Spectre.

The Old War Office Building in Whitehall played the part as MI6 in 1983's Octopussy.

The moment in Die Another Day when Bond enters Vauxhall Cross Underground station was filmed at the end of Westminster Bridge, which also featured in the finale of Spectre.

And the oldest restaurant in London, Rules in Covent Garden, also featured in Spectre, hosting M, Q and Moneypenny.

It still maintains its reputation as a discreet meeting place , allowing customers to live and let dine.

articles.title: Fake faces, stolen voices, false stories: Can we still trust what we see online?
articles.summary: For decades, people have been holding on to the idea that seeing is believing.
articles.body: For decades, people have been holding on to the idea that seeing is believing. Photographs were believed to be the evidence of something happening, videos were believed to be the proof of something, and the known voice on a phone call would prove a person’s identity. However, nowadays, these notions seem to lose their reliability. Artificial intelligence (AI) can produce videos of individuals saying things that they never said, can produce voices using a brief audio recording, and can produce photos of things that did not happen.In times when news spreads all over the world in seconds, differentiating the truth from the fiction becomes a difficult task. Videos shared via WhatsApp, voice messages from family members, and posts on the Internet featuring a famous political leader might be authentic, but they are fake.This is not just a problem of modern technology. This is about a threat for people’s safety, freedom of democracy, credibility of journalism, and the overall public trust.Real-life incidents that show we can no longer believe everything we see online1. Rashmika Mandanna's deepfake video — November 2023October 8, 2023: An original video featuring social media personality Zara Patel was posted on Instagram.November 7, 2023: A manipulated version featuring Rashmika Mandanna's face went viral online.November 10–11, 2023: Delhi Police registered an FIR and began investigating the circulation of the video.The incident raised serious concerns about privacy, online misinformation and the misuse of AI technology. It demonstrated how a person could be falsely portrayed in a video without their knowledge or consent.2. AI voice-cloning scam targeting a mother — March 2024March 18, 2024: A mother from Khargone, Madhya Pradesh, received a phone call claiming that her daughter had been kidnapped.The caller used a voice resembling her daughter's and demanded ₹3 lakh as ransom.The frightened mother transferred ₹50,000 before discovering that her daughter was safe in her hostel.This incident demonstrated how scammers can use AI-generated voices to exploit people's emotions and trick them into transferring money.3. Fake investment video featuring Nirmala Sitharaman — November 2024November 21, 2024: A manipulated video falsely portrayed Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das as endorsing an investment scheme.The video promoted unrealistic financial returns and used manipulated footage and AI-generated audio.Fact-checkers established that the officials had not endorsed the scheme.The incident highlighted how fraudsters can misuse the images and voices of public figures to make fraudulent investment schemes appear trustworthy.These incidents show that videos can be manipulated, voices can be cloned and public figures can be falsely portrayed as endorsing fraudulent schemes. They establish why online content must be verified rather than accepted at face value.Understanding the rise of digital deceptionArtificial intelligence has made it easier than ever to create realistic images, videos, and audio recordings. Deepfake technology can imitate a person’s face, expressions, and voice, making it difficult for viewers to identify whether a video is genuine. At the same time, fake news can spread rapidly through social media, often reaching thousands of people before the truth is established.These developments are concerning because people often trust what they can see and hear. A video of a public figure making a statement or an audio recording of a familiar voice may appear to be reliable evidence, even when it has been manipulated or completely fabricated.AI videos: When the camera can lieAI-generated videos, commonly known as deepfakes, can make people appear to say or do things that never happened. While this technology can be used for entertainment, education, and filmmaking, it can also be misused to spread misinformation, damage reputations, and influence public opinion.For example, a fabricated video of a political leader making a controversial statement could circulate widely before fact-checkers have time to verify it. Even after the video is exposed as fake, the damage may already have been done. Some viewers may continue to believe the original claim, while others may lose trust in genuine recordings.Fake news and the speed of misinformationFake news is not new, but digital platforms have made it easier to create and distribute misleading stories at an extraordinary speed. Sensational headlines, edited images, and false claims can attract attention and be shared before users check their accuracy.Algorithms that recommend engaging content can sometimes contribute to the spread of misinformation. When people repeatedly encounter similar claims, they may begin to accept them as true, even when reliable evidence is missing.The problem is not limited to completely fabricated stories. Genuine photographs and videos can also be taken out of context, edited, or paired with misleading captions to create a false impression.Voice-cloning scams: Hearing is not believingAI voice-cloning tools can reproduce a person’s voice using relatively small amounts of audio. Scammers can exploit this technology to impersonate family members, company executives, or other trusted individuals.Imagine receiving a phone call from someone who sounds exactly like a family member asking for urgent financial help. The familiar voice may make the request seem genuine, causing the listener to act without checking the facts.To protect themselves, people should verify unusual requests through another communication channel, avoid sharing sensitive information over unexpected calls, and be cautious when someone pressures them to transfer money urgently.How to spot misleading contentAlthough AI-generated content is becoming more realistic, there are still steps people can take to assess whether something online is trustworthy.Check the source: Look for the original publisher and check whether reputable news organisations have reported the same information.Verify the context: Check the date, location, and circumstances in which a video or image was supposedly recorded.Look for inconsistencies: Unnatural facial movements, strange lighting, mismatched lip movements, or unusual audio may indicate manipulation, although modern deepfakes may not show obvious flaws.Use reverse image searches: Searching for an image can help reveal whether it appeared earlier in a different context.Read beyond the headline: Sensational headlines may exaggerate or misrepresent the actual content of a report.Pause before sharing: If a claim seems shocking or emotionally charged, verify it before forwarding it to others.Confirm through another channel: For suspicious voice messages or urgent requests for money, contact the person directly using a trusted phone number.No single method can identify every deepfake or misleading post. The most reliable approach is to combine careful observation with independent verification.What can social media platforms do?Social media platforms have an important role in limiting the spread of deceptive content. They can improve systems for detecting manipulated media, label AI-generated content when appropriate, and provide clear information about the origin of images, videos, and audio recordings.Platforms can also work with independent fact-checkers, respond more quickly to reports of harmful misinformation, and make it easier for users to understand why particular content is being recommended. Greater transparency about how content is created and distributed can help people make better-informed decisions.However, automated detection systems are not perfect. Platforms must balance the need to reduce harmful misinformation with the importance of protecting legitimate expression, satire, journalism, and creative uses of AI.Governments, technology companies, news organisations, and users all have a role to play in building a more trustworthy digital environment.Conclusion: Trust, but verifyAs AI technology continues to advance, the boundary between real and fake content will become increasingly difficult to identify. Videos, photographs, and voices can no longer be accepted as unquestionable proof simply because they appear authentic.The solution is not to distrust everything online, but to develop stronger habits of digital awareness. By checking sources, verifying claims, and thinking carefully before sharing information, users can reduce the risk of being misled.In a world where seeing is no longer believing, critical thinking and responsible sharing are essential. Technology may make deception easier, but awareness and verification can help us protect the truth.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: BJP MLA Ritesh Tiwari on Saturday hit out at veteran actor Naseeruddin Shah over his support for protesting students at the Satyajit Ray Film
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BJP MLA Ritesh Tiwari on Saturday hit out at veteran actor Naseeruddin Shah over his support for protesting students at the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute (SRFTI) in Kolkata."Naseeruddin Shah is, by lineage, an opponent of the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Sangh. articles.title: The rise of new black spaces in Bristol's music scene
articles.summary: Young black creatives are continuing a tradition of carving out spaces to dance, connect and belong.
articles.body:
A new sound is taking Bristol's dancefloors by storm.

Driven by rolling log drums, syncopated rhythms and infectious melodies, amapiano and other electronic sounds from across the African diaspora are finding new audiences in a city celebrated for its musical heritage.

Behind these parties is a new generation of black promoters passionate about creating spaces where black people can hear their music, celebrate their cultures and feel like they belong.

But for some, building these spaces has also meant confronting the familiar challenge of finding spaces where black music and the communities around it are welcomed and not feared.

Bristol-based promoter Unkle Mykel's journey into events began in his own back garden after he moved to Bristol in 2017.

What started as garden barbecues gradually grew into a way of bringing people together, particularly members of Bristol's black, Asian and minority ethnic communities.

"It's about celebrating our cultures, bringing people into that fold and connecting," says the 32-year-old, who hosts Bristol Barbecue Family and The Aux Social.

Originally from Kenya, Mykel moved to the UK in 2005. Since then, he has witnessed changes in the visibility of African music.

"There was no Afrobeats on the airwaves," he laughs, recalling his early years in the country, when he says Caribbean reggae, dancehall and soca were more prominent in the musical landscape he encountered.

Now, he sees the growing popularity of genres such as amapiano - a popular South African house music subgenre - as an opportunity to broaden the scene.

"We don't need to pretend to be nobody else, we're just us. It just took a while to get there."

For 30-year-old DJ and promoter Khiah Lou, representation, she says, is central to her work.

Last year she launched Khaya Nights, an event dedicated to amapiano and other African Caribbean electronic dance music.

Having performed internationally, she had seen how other cities had developed a wider range of events celebrating these sounds. Bristol, she felt, was lagging behind.

Rather than wait for the scene to develop, Khiah decided to help build it herself.

"If we don't do it, who else is going to do it?" she says.

"Young black people are starting to make a way for themselves because I don't think we have a choice."

Khiah says these nights provide a place where people can connect with their identities and see their cultures reflected in the city around them.

"At first it seems like it's just a party, but it's so much more than that," she says.

"It's really important for your own self-identity. If your community doesn't have events, where do you feel you can go?"

Tazmin Samuels, who DJs as Azumei, shares those concerns about representation.

As part of Rushtown, a black-led music collective, Tazmin wants to champion sounds and subcultures from across Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean.

"My main motivation for getting together with people and starting Rushtown came from seeing the lack of representation of black music that black people are currently listening to within the city," says Tazmin.

She sees encouraging signs, with more black music-focused brands emerging in Bristol. But she believes the wider music industry has yet to recognise the value of what these promoters are building.

But creating these spaces is not always straightforward.

Khiah says she has struggled to find venues willing to host nights aimed at black audiences. Although she considers Bristol an inclusive city, her experience as a promoter has revealed a different side of its nightlife.

"I've had some venue owners straight up tell me they're worried about having a black event," she says.

"I feel like black crowds are kind of met with fear, and that's really disheartening."

Mykel describes similar tensions, saying that some venues are enthusiastic about hosting his events, only to face objections from people in the surrounding community.

The young promoters' experiences echo a much longer history of black Bristolians having to create their own spaces for music and social life.

Many black people were turned away from existing clubs and bars in Bristol during the 1960s, which led to the creation of "blues parties", un-licensed house parties where people danced to genres such as ska, reggae and rocksteady.

In 1966, Tony Bullimore and his Jamaican-born wife Lalel, opened the Bamboo Club, which served as a cultural lifeline for the city's Caribbean community.

Glen Crooks, 70, who used to perform at the Bamboo Club when he was younger, remembers "sneaking in" with his friends when they were young.

"It was the only place that we could have," he recalls.

"Especially all the Caribbean people could go and really have a good time."

Marti Burgess, who has been a co-owner of the nightclub Lakota since 1994, says although attitudes have changed over the years, some prejudices remain.

"There is a long history of treating a predominantly black audience as a concern, rather than recognising the audience, creativity and business that a promoter is bringing," she says.

"They should not have to keep proving that black audiences are welcome or commercially worthwhile."

Growing up, Marti was surrounded by music. Her parents went to the blues clubs and attended the Bamboo Club when it hosted artists such as Bob Marley, Desmond Dekker and Johnny Nash.

"It was through listening to the adults' conversations that I came to understand how much those spaces had grown out of exclusion from mainstream venues," she says.

"Creating somewhere of their own was both a necessity and a source of joy."

" St Pauls Carnival was hugely important for those of us growing up in the 1970s and 80s, and for our developing identities as Black British people."

Lakota is predominantly known to be a bass music venue, but over the years it has broadened its programme to include Afrobeats and amapiano events.

"Latino Fest this summer opened our eyes further to the audiences and musical communities we could welcome," says Marti.

"We want people across the different genres of black music to see Lakota as a venue that is open to them, where they can bring their music and their audiences."

articles.title: New York woman diagnosed with stage four ovarian cancer at 34 died at 38; her campaign’s first round relieved $44.9 million in medical debt for 51,000 Americans
articles.summary: Casey Ryan McIntyre, a 38-year-old mother from Brooklyn, New York, turned her own experience of cancer care into a campaign to ease the burden of medical
articles.body: Casey Ryan McIntyre, a 38-year-old mother from Brooklyn, New York, turned her own experience of cancer care into a campaign to ease the burden of medical debt on other families. Diagnosed with stage four ovarian cancer at 34, she died on November 12, 2023. Before her death, she arranged a fundraiser to buy and abolish other people’s medical debt, recognising that many Americans lacked the access to good medical care she had received.According to Undue Medical Debt, the campaign’s first round abolished $44.9 million in debt affecting about 51,000 people across nine states. The first round used approximately $300,000 of the more than $1 million raised. The fundraiser began with an original goal of $20,000.Casey McIntyre helped abolish $44.9 million in medical debt for 51,000 peopleThe first round of Casey McIntyre’s memorial campaign abolished $44.9 million in medical debt affecting approximately 51,000 people. The relief was announced on January 16, 2024, by Undue Medical Debt. Approximately $300,000 of the funds raised was used for this initial round, which focused on the Northeast, where McIntyre lived and started her family.The relief reached people across Connecticut, Delaware, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, and Rhode Island. The average amount of debt abolished was $877.How Casey McIntyre’s cancer experience inspired her medical debt relief campaignMcIntyre was diagnosed with stage four ovarian cancer at the age of 34. Her husband, Andrew Rose Gregory, said their medical coverage made their experience of cancer care easier than that of many other families. He described how cancer patients across the United States were postponing or refusing care, or taking on substantial medical debt because they lacked coverage.Their experience of the healthcare system, alongside their awareness of their own access to good coverage, inspired them to create a debt jubilee as part of McIntyre’s posthumous memorial. In announcing her death on her X account, McIntyre said she had arranged to buy up and destroy other people’s medical debt to celebrate her life.Casey McIntyre’s $20,000 fundraiser grew into a campaign worth over $1 millionThe original goal of McIntyre’s fundraiser was $20,000, but the campaign raised more than $1 million towards eliminating medical debt through Undue Medical Debt. Gregory said the family had never imagined that the initiative would raise so much or that McIntyre’s story would reach so many people. Initially, he saw the campaign as a way for his family to free others from the burden of medical debt. Over time, he came to see it as a way to create opportunities for those receiving relief. He said the relief could give families greater freedom to pursue better jobs, move into better homes, buy a new car, or work towards a long-held dream of earning a degree or certification.How the nonprofit identifies people eligible for medical debt reliefUndue Medical Debt works to relieve the burden of medical debt and improve people’s economic opportunities and ability to live healthier lives. Its eligibility criteria cover individuals whose incomes are at or below four times the federal poverty level, as well as those whose medical debt accounts for 5% or more of their gross annual income.The nonprofit states that medical debt relief cannot be requested by individuals because its process is source-based. As of January 2024, the organisation had abolished more than $10.4 billion in medical debt since its establishment in 2014, helping more than seven million people.You use AI every day. articles.title: Helen Mirren, 81, is on a mission to save Italy’s 1,500-year-old olive trees; deadly Xylella fastidiosa bacteria has wiped out 22 million trees since 2013; 'We have to save these trees,' she says
articles.summary: Oscar-winning actor Dame Helen Mirren has spent decades entertaining audiences with her performances, but one of her most important missions lies far from
articles.body: Oscar-winning actor Dame Helen Mirren has spent decades entertaining audiences with her performances, but one of her most important missions lies far from the film sets. The 81-year-old actor is fighting to save Italy’s ancient olive trees from a devastating bacterial infection that has wiped out millions of trees and caused billions of euros in economic damage.For nearly a decade, Mirren has been raising awareness about Xylella fastidiosa, an invasive bacterium that has devastated olive groves in southern Italy. Through her initiative, Save the Olives, she hopes to protect trees that have survived for centuries and preserve an important part of Italy’s cultural, environmental and economic heritage.Speaking to PEOPLE, the MobLand star expressed concern over the lack of attention being paid to the crisis. “It's amazing how people want to put on blinkers and pretend it's not happening,” she said.Helen Mirren’s connection to Italy’s olive treesMirren’s fight is deeply personal. In 2007, she and her husband, filmmaker Taylor Hackford, bought a 16th-century farmhouse in Puglia, in southeastern Italy. The couple’s home is surrounded by the region’s olive-growing landscape, which has been severely affected by the spread of Xylella.The bacterium was first detected in southern Italy in 2013, according to the science journal Nature. Since then, estimates suggest that around 22 million olive trees have been lost to the disease.Xylella spreads between plants through certain insects, including spittlebugs. When the infection reached areas near Mirren’s home, she initially believed the threat would not become as serious as it eventually did.“We - just like everybody else - thought, ‘Oh, it won't come to us.’ And it did,” she recalled. “It killed all of the trees.”The experience prompted Mirren and others to take action, leading to the creation of Save the Olives.Why Helen Mirren co-founded Save the OlivesMirren said the initiative initially focused on providing reliable information about the disease and countering misinformation surrounding the crisis.“We started Save the Olives just as a way of getting information out there. Because as always happens with things like this, disinformation starts flying around and bad theories, wrong theories,” she explained.The organisation aims to encourage people to recognise the scale of the problem and support efforts to protect the surviving trees.“We are just really fighting for people to please pay attention and realize that yes, this is happening and you are going to lose 1,500-year-old trees,” Mirren said.“And when you think that this living thing has been in the earth living, surviving since the Romans, come on! We have to save these trees.”For Mirren, the loss goes beyond the destruction of individual plants. These ancient olive trees represent centuries of history, connecting present-day communities with generations that came before them.How people can help save the ancient olive treesSave the Olives has introduced a tree-adoption programme that allows people to contribute directly to conservation efforts. A donation of €500, approximately $560, can fund a lengthy and expensive process in which varieties of bacteria-resistant olive trees are grafted onto endangered trees.According to the organisation, people who adopt a tree can name it and receive photographs and its GPS location. Those who wish to contribute can also make donations in other amounts.Mirren said the initiative is working alongside efforts to develop new olive varieties that can withstand the disease while producing high-quality olive oil.“We're doing that, and then we are also developing new species that produce great olive oil, because that's really important,” she said.The work is particularly significant because olive oil production plays a major role in Italy’s economy. The destruction of olive groves has affected agricultural output, livelihoods and local communities, with the economic damage estimated in the billions of euros.“Producing oil is one of Italy's major economic things,” Mirren said. “So it's really, really serious.”Helen Mirren remains hopeful about the futureDespite the scale of the devastation, Mirren remains hopeful that conservation efforts and the development of resistant olive varieties can help protect the remaining trees.Her campaign combines environmental preservation with the need to safeguard Italy’s agricultural traditions and the livelihoods of those who depend on olive cultivation.For the veteran actor, the cause is also about recognising the extraordinary resilience of these trees, many of which have survived for more than a millennium.“They're one of the most miraculous things on this planet,” she said.You use AI every day. articles.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has warned of a “big surprise” for the Palestinian Authority (PA), a day after two Israeli soldiers were killed in a Palestinian gun attack in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron.In an interview with i24 News late Friday, Netanyahu suggested that Israel could launch a major military operation against the Palestinian Authority, which governs parts of the West Bank in coordination with Israel under agreements reached in the 1990s.“I will act to neutralize that threat by means I think are better left unspecified right now,” Netanyahu said when asked whether he supported calls to dismantle the PA.“There is a very big surprise for the Palestinian Authority as well,” he added.Netanyahu's remarks came after he said the Israel Defence Forces (IDF) had prepared plans for a large-scale operation in the West Bank, which Israel refers to as Judea and Samaria.“The IDF is ready to carry it out, and we will determine the timing, but it is on its way,” he said on Friday, describing the proposed campaign as unprecedented in scale since the Six-Day War.The Israeli prime minister also referred to Israel's military operations in Gaza, Lebanon, Syria and Iran, claiming that his government had reshaped the region.“We transformed the Middle East. I said that we would change things and we have,” Netanyahu said.Meanwhile, Israeli forces imposed widespread restrictions across Hebron on Saturday following the attack that killed two soldiers. All gates leading into and out of the city were reportedly closed to vehicles, forcing Palestinians to cross on foot.Israeli troops also ordered residents to leave their homes in parts of the city. articles.summary: Connor Weigman's 20 touchdown passes meet Devon Dampier's dual-threat ability as No. 14 Houston Cougars face No. 10 Utah Utes in a Big 12 showdown.
articles.body: There are just two ranked matchups today, and one of those was between two SEC big shots, and then this one between two Big 12 teams. The Big 12 hasn’t gotten a ton of love this season, but there are four teams in the top 14 of the national rankings. You could make an argument that this is the best conference in college football. It wouldn’t be a great argument, but you could make it. Tonight we have Houston taking on Utah in one of the best matchups of the day. The Houston Cougars come into the game with a 3-1 record and as the 14th-ranked team in the country. Their lone loss this year was against Texas Tech in a very close road game. They lost the game 28-26, clearly putting up a strong fight. It hasn’t been completely smooth sailing for the team, though. They’ve won the past four weeks, beating Georgia Southern by 14 points, then UCF by 10 the following week. In the past two weeks, the team has taken down Kansas State and Oklahoma State. Against Kansas State, they won by 19 points on the road. Against the Cowboys, they won by just three. In fairness to Houston, they entered the fourth quarter with an 11-point lead over Oklahoma State. The Cowboys put up 14 points in the quarter, but a Houston touchdown gave them a lead Oklahoma State could never get passed. THE SEC MIGHT HAVE MORE HEADLINERS, BUT THE BIG 12 HAS THE MOST UNDERRATED MATCHUP OF WEEK 4 The Utah Utes, the worst-named team in football, are 6-0 and the 10th-ranked team in the country. This will be the toughest game they’ve played to date, and it might be one they were already focused. Last week they took on Colorado on the road, but won 27-24. I think Utah might’ve already been thinking about this game, because the Buffaloes aren’t even close to being as good as the Utes. Sometimes teams just have bad games, but that’s okay. Utah has also beaten Kansas, Iowa State, Utah State, Arkansas, and Idaho this season. The only game that was within one score was the Colorado game. Their next closest game was against Iowa State, also a road game, where they still won by 14 points. At home this season, they’ve won by an average of 33.8 points. Their team is built around quarterback Devon Dampier. He has completed about 69% of passes this season with 15 touchdowns and four interceptions. He has also run for another three scores this season. He does a bit of everything for the team, and Houston will have their hands full trying to stop him. HOUSTON RALLIES FOR COMEBACK VICTORY OVER UCF IN FRONT OF A PAINFULLY SPARSE HOME CROWD This game features two really good offenses. Connor Weigman from the Cougars is one of the better quarterbacks in the league. He has 20 touchdown passes this season in seven games. Dampier might be slowed down a bit, but I doubt he can be stopped altogether. I expect the two teams to both challenge all three levels repeatedly. I’m going to take the over 56.5 in this game. articles.title: British woman dies trying to rescue sons swept away by strong current while snorkelling in Bahamas
articles.summary: A British woman has died while trying to rescue her two sons after they were swept away by a strong current while snorkelling in the Bahamas.
articles.body: A British woman has died while trying to rescue her two sons after they were swept away by a strong current while snorkelling in the Bahamas.According to the BBC, the 36-year-old woman, believed to be from Stapleford in Nottinghamshire, was snorkelling with her husband and two sons near the southern point of North Bimini island on Tuesday when the incident occurred.The Royal Bahamas Police Force said the current reportedly swept both children away, prompting their mother to attempt a rescue. She was also swept away, while the two boys were later rescued from the water.Police said officers at the Alice Town police station received information shortly after 10am that a woman was unresponsive at the North Bimini ferry dock. She was taken to a local clinic, where a doctor pronounced her dead despite efforts to save her life.The woman was reportedly rescued from the water and brought to the ferry dock, where CPR was administered. Police said foul play was not suspected and an autopsy would be conducted to determine the exact cause of death.The British Foreign Office said it was in contact with local authorities and providing support to the woman's family."Our thoughts are with the family of a British woman who has died in the Bahamas," a Foreign Office spokesperson said.Bimini is a small island group in the Bahamas, located close to the US mainland. North Bimini is home to Alice Town, one of the main settlements on the island.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Can no longer breathe': Thousands protest in Turkey over media crackdown, jailed journalists
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Thousands of people took to the streets in Istanbul and Ankara on Saturday to protest what journalists and rights groups described as growing
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Thousands of people took to the streets in Istanbul and Ankara on Saturday to protest what journalists and rights groups described as growing government pressure on independent media, including arrests, censorship and the takeover of news outlets.Police estimated that around 3,000 people attended the demonstration in Ankara. Journalists, rights activists and opposition representatives joined the protests, chanting slogans such as “Enough!” and “We can no longer breathe!” and demanding press freedom and the release of jailed journalists, as reported by AFP.In Istanbul, demonstrators displayed photographs of imprisoned journalists and shouted, “We will not be silenced. Enough is enough!” and “We will not bow to pressure”.The protests come amid growing concerns over restrictions on independent journalism in Turkey. According to the Turkish Journalists' Union, authorities have jailed 11 journalists over the past two months and shut down several media outlets.Earlier this month, police raided Halk TV, Turkey's most-watched news channel, halted its broadcasts and installed a government-appointed administrator. The move was the latest action against media organisations perceived to be critical of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his government.Authorities also shut down the website and social media accounts of digital news outlet T24 over what they described as “LGBT propaganda”.Press freedom has faced increasing constraints in Turkey since a failed coup attempt in 2016, with journalists subjected to prosecutions and digital censorship. Authorities have also accused media professionals of spreading fake news.Veteran journalist Zafer Arapkirli, speaking after the Istanbul demonstration, said the protests were about defending the public's right to information as well as journalists' freedom.“This gathering is not simply about standing up for journalists,” he told AFP. “It is also about defending respect for society's right to access information and news through journalists and independent media.”Arapkirli, who himself faces lawsuits, accused the authorities of using arrests and restrictions to intimidate the public. “What the regime wants is to intimidate, silence and frighten society through such pressure -- by arresting individual journalists, seizing media outlets, banning news coverage and blocking access to social media,” he said.“We must show that we will not allow this to happen,” he added.Gokhan Durmus, president of the Turkish Journalists' Union, said recent restrictions had increasingly targeted prominent broadcasters and widely followed news platforms.“We are seeing a system emerge in which everything is uniform: one voice, one source of news, one centralised operation,” he told AFP.In Ankara, demonstrators called for an end to censorship and demanded the release of journalists in prison. Gokcer Tahincioglu of the shut-down outlet T24 said the rally defended both journalists' rights and the public's access to information.“Journalists are determined to get one message across: we want to practise journalism, and we want to be able to do so freely,” he said.A letter from jailed BirGun journalist Ismail Ari was also read out at the Ankara protest. Ari, who was arrested this month for the second time in seven months, said he had been imprisoned for carrying out his work.“I am being held in prison for no reason other than doing my job as a journalist. Days are being stolen from my life,” he wrote from Sincan prison on the outskirts of Ankara.“We will defend journalism to the very end. Take your hands off us, comply with the constitution and let us do our job,” he added.Ari faces charges of insulting a public official and publicly disseminating misleading information following a complaint by Turkey's broadcasting watchdog chief, Ebubekir Sahin.The Turkish government has repeatedly denied that journalists are arrested or imprisoned for doing their jobs.You use AI every day.
